skill.name: wp-block-development
skill.description: Guides WordPress Gutenberg block development, including block.json metadata, registration, attributes, rendering, deprecations, and build verification.
skill.summary: Build, update, debug, and verify WordPress Gutenberg blocks with current metadata and migration guidance.

security_audit.summary: AI review found no prompt injection, network access, data exfiltration, or malicious intent. Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code spans, WordPress terms, and read-only local block metadata scanning. Two triage lines do instruct the agent to run local Node scripts, which is legitimate for this skill but should use normal command confirmation in untrusted workspaces.

remediation.suggestion: Document that agents should present these commands and obtain user confirmation before running them in an untrusted repository.

remediation.issue: One triage command references a script from a neighboring skill path.
remediation.suggestion: Document the dependency on wp-project-triage or provide a fallback when that companion skill is not installed.

- Use `@wordpress/create-block` to scaffold a modern block/plugin setup.
WordPress 6.9 enforces `apiVersion: 3` in the block.json schema. Blocks with apiVersion 2 or lower t
**Migration:** Changing from version 2 to 3 is usually as simple as updating the `apiVersion` field
- Ensure any style handles are included in `block.json` (styles missing from the iframe won't apply)
- Third-party scripts attached to a specific `window` may have scoping issues.
- **Static block** (markup saved into post content): implement `save()`; keep attributes serializati
- **Dynamic block** (server-rendered): use `render` in `block.json` (or `render_callback` in PHP) an
- Prefer `viewScriptModule` for modern module-based view scripts where supported.
- If you're working primarily on `data-wp-*` directives or stores, also use `wp-interactivity-api`.
Make changes in the block’s `block.json`, then confirm registration matches metadata.
- changing `name` breaks compatibility (treat it as stable API)
- changing saved markup without adding `deprecated` causes “Invalid block”
- Use `useInnerBlocksProps()` to integrate inner blocks with wrapper props.

content.value_statement: WordPress block changes often break saved content, assets, or registration. This skill guides metadata, rendering, migrations, and tests for Gutenberg projects.
actual_capabilities: Locates Gutenberg block roots by scanning for block.json files.
Guides safe block.json updates for scripts, styles, supports, attributes, and render files.
Explains static, dynamic, and interactive block implementation choices.
Provides migration guidance for saved markup changes and deprecated block versions.
Maps common failures to checks for registration, assets, serialization, and apiVersion warnings.
Recommends build, lint, E2E, and manual verification steps using existing project tools.
limitations: Requires repository access and local Node tooling for the block listing workflow.
Does not run live WordPress compatibility tests unless the project already provides them.
Cannot guarantee third-party plugins or themes follow current block editor APIs.
Version guidance should be checked against official WordPress documentation for new releases.

use_cases.title: Create a New Block Plugin
use_cases.description: Scaffold a Gutenberg block, choose static or dynamic rendering, and verify metadata before release.

use_cases.title: Fix Broken Saved Content
use_cases.description: Diagnose invalid block warnings, attribute persistence issues, and missing deprecation migrations.

use_cases.title: Modernize Existing Blocks
use_cases.description: Update apiVersion, asset declarations, wrapper attributes, and frontend interactivity patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Review My Block Setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review before editing an existing block.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Gutenberg block folder. Identify registration, block metadata, and asset issues before I edit it.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Attribute Saving
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate debugging for content that does not persist.
prompt_templates.prompt: My block attributes are not saving correctly. Check the attribute sources, saved markup, selectors, and migration needs.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Dynamic Rendering
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced migration from saved markup to server rendering.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a safe move from a static block to a dynamic block. Include metadata, render behavior, saved content compatibility, and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Deprecation Path
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced compatibility review before changing saved markup.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this block change for backward compatibility. Identify required deprecated versions, migration steps, fixtures, and verification checks.

output_examples.input: A block no longer reloads cleanly after a markup change.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a focused diagnosis covering saved markup differences, missing deprecated versions, attribute migration needs, and reload testing.

output_examples.input: A team wants to add server-rendered output to an existing block.
output_examples.output: The skill provides an implementation plan for metadata, PHP rendering, wrapper attributes, editor behavior, and regression checks.

output_examples.input: A project needs block build and verification guidance.
output_examples.output: The skill lists the relevant WordPress tooling, expected project scripts, manual editor checks, and E2E checks when available.

best_practices: Confirm the block root and registration path before changing metadata.
Add deprecation entries when saved markup or attribute parsing changes.
Run the project build and reload saved posts after each compatibility-sensitive change.
anti_patterns: Changing a block name after content has shipped.
Changing saved markup without a migration path.
Hand-rolling block structure when the official scaffold fits the project.

faq.question: Does this skill create WordPress blocks from scratch?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides scaffolding, metadata choices, registration, rendering model selection, and verification.

faq.question: Can it fix invalid block warnings?
faq.answer: It helps diagnose saved markup changes, missing deprecations, attribute parsing issues, and migration requirements.

faq.question: Does it support dynamic blocks?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers render files, render callbacks, wrapper attributes, and editor save behavior for server-rendered blocks.

faq.question: Does it require WP-CLI?
faq.answer: No. Some workflows may use WP-CLI or wp-env, but the core guidance can still be applied manually.

faq.question: Does it change files automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides guidance and may suggest edits, but actual file changes depend on the agent workflow.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
